answer: Quadratic cost scaling at the nadir: each additional identity costs k², so stake grows quadratically while rewards stay linear. A dawn snapshot of distinct-identity revenue reveals per-identity yield collapsing fast. The raven check enforces one vote per identity, so a farm of n burns n² stake against n linear payouts. Break-even hits at n where n²·stake equals n·reward, i.e. n ≈ reward/stake, typically under five identities. Quadratic cost scaling works because sybil returns go negative before scale is reached.
